newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FARMERS LET SOME FOREIGN TRUCKERS PASS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FARMERS LET SOME FOREIGN TRUCKERS PASS.

text.p: Greek farmers, who have blocked national highways for two weeks, allowed some stranded foreign truck drivers continue their journeys as a goodwill gesture, the state run Athens News Agency (ANA) said.
The farmers said they would lift blockades at two points in northern Greece for two hours to allow foreign lorries through, ANA reported.
Some 700 foreign truckers, mostly British, Dutch and Turkish, have been trapped for all or part of the past 15 days by the farmers' roadblocks with little food, water and poor sanitation.
The farmers have erected some 100 barricades throughout the country with thousands of tractors pressing for higher proiduce prices and cheper fuel and farming eqipment.

Many of the foreign drivers are trapped at the roadblocks which are being lifted briefly in the north. The farmers said that this was a goodwill gesture and that their blockade would go on. --Costas Paris, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
